correctness.rationale: In the centered coordinate simplex, expanding the ball inequality cancels the 1/m on both sides and gives lambda_i>=Q, Q=sum lambda_j^2; the maximum coordinate always qualifies. Under the normalized-exponential coupling the test is E_i>=T_m, T_m=sum E_i^2/sum E_i. The strong law gives T_m->2, and bracketing by empirical survivals at deterministic thresholds gives almost-sure convergence to p=e^(-2). The ratio linearization uses H=E^2-2E. On a window of radius K/sqrt(m) the proof's grid has O(m^(1/4)) points, the centered survival increment has variance O(m^(-3/2)) at each grid point, and a binomial count bound in each grid interval controls interpolation. This justifies the local empirical-process expansion at T_m. For I=1{E>=2}, integration of -(x^2 exp(-x))' gives Cov(I,H)=4p and factorial moments give Var(H)=8, so the influence I-p-pH has variance p(1-p). This is a Gaussian limit, not a finite-sample binomial model. The supplied checker and notes were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Write U_m=(N_m(2/m)-mp)/sqrt(m) and V_m=sqrt(m)(mG-2). The two exponential thresholds differ by (mG-2) times the sample mean, and the derivative of the population survival at 2 is -p. The prior proof's local equicontinuity thus gives (N_m(G)-mp)/sqrt(m)=U_m-pV_m+o_P(1). The joint limit has zero cross term, so the variance is [p(1-p)-4p^2]+4p^2.
The strong law follows from the same normalized-exponential representation plus deterministic bracketing; it does not add a distinct nontrivial asymptotic mechanism.
